instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Supportive Rage
cards.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get this paint off my sofa. Take the cloth; we'll do it calmly and you won't be left to manage it alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the carpet too. I don't think rubbing is helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then blot it your way. Good thinking. That carpet was my birthday present, so let's be very bloody careful with it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cloth's full of paint. We need something clean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use my shirt. Yes, the clean one I was saving. I'll hold the stained cloth out of your way; you're doing well, and I am furious enough to keep holding it all afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll organize the birthday lunch you really want. Choose the place and I'll get us there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The seaside one. But you'd lose your deposit here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forty pounds gone. Fine. You love the sea; I'll make the drive part of the treat. You choose the route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it. They need another forty to hold the window table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another forty? Eighty bloody pounds before lunch. Give me the number; I'm paying for your sea view. Ask them for the best window, and don't you settle for a view of the bins.

cards.title: Terms and Conditions
cards.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sort the ladder loan out. Two lifts to the station and it's yours for the afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need it for five minutes. Two lifts is too much.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One, then. I can make a sensible adjustment. You choose the morning and I'll be ready at the kerb.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather pay you than promise a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five pounds will settle it. Three if you hand it over with 'thanks, friend.' We can call that my regular-customer rate if you prefer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can settle your apology for missing my birthday. Give me first choice of a Christmas visit and I'll put the hurt behind us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum already has Christmas Day. I can't promise you that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Boxing Day will suit my plan nicely. You choose the train; I'll tell Mum we're all right again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather you actually felt all right than just told her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me the whole weekend, and I'll work on feeling it. You can choose what we do; in return, I won't bring the birthday up while you're here.

cards.title: Yes, but My Way
cards.instruction: Agree with others, then reinterpret the agreement entirely in your favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll help move the sofa. I'll organize the lift and take the cushions first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're sewn on. We both have to get underneath it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely, we'll work together. You choose the pace; I'll give the count while you get a grip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need a second person actually lifting, not counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. You choose someone you trust and I'll arrange the time with them. Then I can give you both the count at your pace. That's a much better version of helping together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll look after your dog while the kitchen's repaired. I'll make the arrangements; bring him after his walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll need to stay overnight too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. You can have the guest room with him. Choose whichever bedding he likes; I'll leave breakfast ready for you both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll stay, but the six o'clock walk is yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed, I'll organize it around you. You choose the route; I'll put the lead by your shoes and set your alarm. All you'll have to do is take him out.

cards.title: The Pattern
cards.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get to the bottom of these missing biscuits. Two gone at once suggests an organized operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ate them. Please don't turn it into an investigation about me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, no names. A quick admission like that suggests people have learned to protect the system. Just tell me what made you take them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was hungry. Lunch was late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll look at the timetable, not you. You can choose how we ask the others. If hunger is organizing the office, this is much bigger than a biscuit tin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sort this communication failure out. Nobody got my meeting email; the whole office is working blind.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in your drafts. You forgot to press send.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. You can check the outgoing messages with me. A system that depends on one finger is more fragile than I thought.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll press send. Go and eat your lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, you can cover this end. Choose the handover note and I'll follow it. If one sandwich needs a deputy, we must have an entire succession problem waiting in the canteen.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll have this shelf up before you leave. Could you hold the bracket against those holes for a moment?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Briefly. I'm dressed for work and I don't want dust on me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll catch the dust. Could you turn the top screw once so you can take your hand away?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's holding now. The other screws are lined up too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Just tighten those while they're ready, then slide the shelf on to check. I'll brush your sleeve and fetch your coat; we've kept the job moving beautifully.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll finish this wedding bouquet neatly. Could you pinch the stems while I settle the ribbon?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ribbon will slip. You need wire underneath it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly the adjustment I wanted. You know the grip already; could you twist this wire round while I keep the ribbon clear?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done, but the sharp end will catch the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. Tuck that end in, then wind the ribbon over it; one small bow should finish it. You choose the knot and I'll hold the scissors out of your way.
